thread:
liao: 🔴 na-east1 control-plane: provisioner appears stuck, trying to create GPU nodes but requests are queuing and auth/routing degraded. seeing 503s from auth-proxy. ops runbook says failover if provisioning > 5m.
oncall-bot: Alert: NA-EAST1_PROVISIONER_STALL at 2026-03-18T10:14:28Z — severity: high. @oncall paging.
jia: Can you paste the provisioner logs and the auth-proxy error? is the cluster flapping or just the queue? :thinking:
liao: logs (tail):
```
2026-03-18T10:12:10 provisioner INFO claim: pod x pending due to insufficient GPUs
2026-03-18T10:12:15 provisioner ERROR allocate: deadlock acquiring host-lock: timeout
2026-03-18T10:12:20 controlplane/cache WARN kv-sync stalled for 24s
2026-03-18T10:13:00 auth-proxy ERROR 503 upstream_unavailable
```
ken: Sounds like the provisioning engine hit a lock in the controlplane cache write path. That explains auth hits — token fetches depend on kv-sync. First action: divert new traffic to na-west1 and scale up west burst nodes. We can also evict queued provisioning requests temporarily.
sam: Current capacity snapshot: na-east1 GPUs healthy: 0 allocatable. na-west1 available GPUs: 240 (60 idle). eu-west1 available GPUs: 120 (30 idle). If we shift ~20% of traffic to na-west1 we should be fine. Cost impact estimate: +8-12% on GPU hourly until routes converge.
liao: @ken how do we evict queue safely? runbook step 3 uses `kubectl exec provisioner -- evict-queue --dry-run` then non-dry-run. I'm prepping the command.
ken: Do dry-run first, then non-dry-run. Also trigger routing fallback: update routing policy `controlplane.route_policy=failover-na-west1` via flagroll in controlplane — small window will see 429->503 if done incorrectly. I can push the flagroll if you need.
liao: Doing dry-run now:
```
kubectl -n infra exec provisioner-0 -- ./provisioner evict-queue --dry-run
# result: 83 queued requests would be requeued to fallback
```
liao: Proceeding with non-dry-run.
ops-bot: Runbook action executed by liao: provisioner-evict-queue -> success. 83 requests requeued to fallback routing.
dev-console: Console sessions are degraded — some users can't open instance pages due to controlplane kv read timeouts. After failover we should see console reconnects. Monitoring: auth 503s dropped ~70% after routing change.
jia: Good. Next: we still need a root cause. Ken, can you capture a heap/profile of the provisioner and controlplane cache process and open a ticket? add `--profile=true` and upload to S3.
ken: Will do. Also scheduling a rolling restart of provisioner pods one at a time to break the lock. Command: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/provisioner --timeout=5m` — doing now.
ops-bot: rollout restart started for deployment/provisioner.
liao: Auth errors trending down, console reconnect rate up. We'll leave traffic shifted to na-west1 for 30 minutes and watch. Postmortem to include: why cache lock occurred, why GPU host-lock deadlock allowed 83 queued requests, and why controlplane routing didn't fallback earlier.
sam: Noted. Cost/ops impact: rough estimate for the 45-minute failover + burst capacity = ~$1.9k extra GPU spend. Flagging to finance.
jia: Thanks everyone. I'll create the incident ticket with timeline and collect logs/profiles. assign @ken for RCA and @liao for mitigation notes. :thumbsup:
